profile.text: India's largest private hospital group: 48 owned hospitals plus 6 managed, 9,857 census beds in its network (owned, managed and AHLL; 11,147 capacity) and 8,352 operating beds incl. the 22%-owned Delhi hospital (Jun-2026). Three reported businesses: Healthcare Services (hospitals, 50% of FY26 revenue and 81% of EBITDA), Apollo HealthCo (pharmacy distribution to ~7,440 Apollo pharmacies plus the Apollo 24/7 digital platform, 43% of revenue) and Apollo Health & Lifestyle (AHLL: clinics, diagnostics, Spectra day surgery, dialysis, Cradle and fertility, 7%). Founded in 1983 by Dr Prathap C. Reddy (first hospital in Chennai); the Reddy family owns 28%.

segments.name: Healthcare Services (hospitals)
segments.note: Consolidated hospitals; the Delhi (Indraprastha) hospital is a 22% associate and only its profit share is consolidated. ROCE 25.4% in FY26 and 28.5% in Q1FY27 on capital employed excl. CWIP (company).

segments.name: Apollo HealthCo (offline pharmacy distribution, online pharmacy, Apollo 24/7)
segments.note: HealthCo supplies the Apollo pharmacy stores, which are owned by Apollo Medicals (AMPL) and not consolidated; it also runs Apollo 24/7 (49 mn registered users, ~8 lakh daily active users, GMV Rs535 cr in Q1FY27, +23%). Digital cash loss Rs10 cr in Q1FY27 vs Rs49 cr a year earlier; breakeven guided for Q2FY27.

segments.name: Apollo Health & Lifestyle (AHLL)
segments.note: Q1FY27 network: 299 clinics, 172 dialysis centres, 294 dental centres, ~2,894 diagnostic collection points. Diagnostics revenue +31% and EBITDA +136% in Q1FY27; management targets 20%+ growth and ~20% diagnostics margin within 6-8 quarters. AHLL became 100% owned in Mar-2026 (Rs1,273 cr paid to IFC and other minorities).

q1fy27.growthSplit: Established hospitals +18% (volume +11%, price +4%, case/payer mix +3%); new hospitals Rs92 cr of revenue and an EBITDA loss of Rs38 cr; established-hospital EBITDA margin 25.9%.

payerMix.note: Share of in-patient revenue. Insurance revenue +25%, self-pay +16%, international +26% in Q1FY27.

callPoints: Hospital revenue growth of ~20% in FY27 'on track' (MD); 18-20% for the year (CFO). Established hospitals to grow 13-14% a year (7-8% volume) and new hospitals to add ~7% over the next 24 months.
Established-hospital margin of ~26% is 'a good sustainable number' (CFO); margins to 'inch up a bit' over 24 months.

New-hospital losses ~Rs150 cr for FY27, rising by ~Rs20 cr a quarter when Gurgaon opens (soft launch Sep-2026, opening Oct-2026, revenue from Q4FY27); Hyderabad Financial District to break even in Q2FY27; the new-hospital cluster to break even by Q3-Q4 FY28.
Pricing: ~5% a year ('medical inflation'); insurance contracts reset every two years. 70% of patients pay under Rs2 lakh per admission.
Bangladesh in-patient volumes back to 60-70% of their peak; international revenue +26%.
Digital (24/7) cash breakeven expected in Q2FY27; insurance broking breakeven by end-Q3FY27; steady-state 24/7 cost ~Rs80 cr a quarter.
Payer mix: cash + insurance at ~85% 'very maintained' even outside the South.
MD on the Parliamentary committee's pricing recommendations: price controls 'may dis-incentivise investments'; tariff increases mirror inflation.

fy26.exceptionalNote: Provision for higher gratuity and leave liabilities under the New Labour Code (effective 21-Nov-2025).

minorities.note: Profit allocated to non-controlling interests, FY26, Rs cr (AR FY26 consolidated note 21): hospital subsidiaries Assam 23.8% minority, Apollomedics Lucknow 49%, AHIL Ahmedabad 50%, Imperial Bengaluru 10%, Apollo Rajshree Indore 45.37%, Apollo Nellore 19.13%, Apollo Lavasa 49%, Kerala First 40% = Rs57.4 cr; AHLL line Rs5.7 cr (AHLL 100% owned from Mar-2026; residual is step-down subsidiaries); Apollo HealthCo 0.32% Rs1.1 cr; Apollo Home Healthcare 26% Rs2.1 cr; Health Axis 30.01% -Rs5.3 cr; Sapien 30% ~0. Total Rs61.0 cr. Q1FY27 total Rs29.7 cr, not disclosed by entity.

expansion.summary: Census beds 9,857 (Jun-2026) to ~14,100 by FY31 (+4,330 census beds, +5,798 total beds) for a project cost of ~Rs11,150 cr, of which ~Rs7,500 cr was still to be spent at Jun-2026 (Rs3,650 cr already incurred, per ICICI Direct). 380 of ~1,000 recently commissioned census beds (excluding Gurgaon) were operational at Jun-2026; the other ~620 to open over 12-18 months.

projects.name: Gurgaon, NCR
projects.note: Soft launch Sep-2026, opening Oct-2026 (Q1FY27 call)

restructuring.text: Composite scheme (announced end-Jun-2025): Apollo's omni-channel pharmacy distribution and Apollo 24/7 (its shares in Apollo HealthCo) and the AHEL telehealth division are demerged into a new company (Apollo Healthtech Ltd); Apollo HealthCo and Keimed (the promoter-linked pharmaceutical wholesaler) then merge into it. AHEL shareholders receive 195.2 NewCo shares per 100 AHEL shares. Resulting NewCo: AHEL shareholders 42.1% directly, AHEL 15% plus ~2.5% economic interest through its 49% stake in FHPL (so 59.6% for AHEL and its shareholders combined), Advent 12.1%, ESOP 3.0%, Keimed promoters and others 25.3%. NewCo owns 25.5% of AMPL, holding company of the Apollo Pharmacies store chain. NCLT Chennai convened the meetings (order of 26-Mar-2026); shareholders approved the scheme on 24-Jun-2026; final NCLT sanction and listing are pending, with listing estimated by Q4FY27 'post all approvals'. Advent International invested Rs2,475 cr in Apollo HealthCo through CCPS (Sep-2024 and Mar-2025); the CCPS sit in consolidated borrowings (Rs2,457 cr at Mar-26) and convert when the scheme takes effect. The proceeds funded purchases of Keimed shares (Rs800 cr at fair value in investments, Mar-26).

cloudnine.text: AHLL is combining Apollo Cradle and Apollo Fertility with Cloudnine (Kids Clinic India Ltd): valued at ~Rs1,550 cr (~35x FY26 IGAAP EBITDA of Rs45 cr on Rs450 cr revenue), paid in cash (~Rs750 cr, to be redeployed in primary care) and a 9.9% fully diluted stake in Cloudnine. Announced 20-May-2026; CCI approved on 1-Sep-2026; management expected completion in Q2FY27.

cash.note: Company net debt excludes lease liabilities and the Advent CCPS. Screener 'borrowings' (Rs8,493 cr at Mar-26) = bank and other debt Rs3,202 cr + CCPS Rs2,457 cr + leases Rs2,834 cr. Screener cash + investments (Rs3,296 cr) = company cash and treasury Rs2,336 cr + strategic stakes (Keimed Rs800 cr, IMCL Rs179 cr at equity-method book, FHPL Rs60 cr, others).
cash.src: AR FY26 notes 10, 11, 22, 23; Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 presentations

history.event: Dr Prathap C. Reddy opens Apollo's first hospital in Chennai, India's first corporate hospital.
history.impact: Founder-led group; the Reddy family (four daughters run the businesses) still controls it with 28%.

history.event: Covid year: revenue -6%, EBITDA -28%; equity raised through a QIP (share capital Rs70 cr to Rs72 cr).
history.impact: FY21 is a trough year in the history (EPS Rs10.5).

history.event: Pharmacy restructuring: the front-end store chain moved to Apollo Medicals (AMPL, an associate); Apollo HealthCo formed in Mar-2022 to run back-end distribution and Apollo 24/7. Covid vaccination and testing revenue boosted FY22.
history.impact: HealthCo revenue is wholesale distribution, so its margins look thin (8-9% before digital costs). FY22 PAT included Rs220 cr of exceptional gains.

history.event: Apollo 24/7 build-out: digital operating costs of Rs657 cr (FY23), Rs619 cr (FY24) and Rs478 cr (FY25) pushed HealthCo EBITDA negative in FY23-24.
history.impact: Group EBITDA margin 12.3-12.5% in FY23-24 vs 13.9% in FY25 and 14.9% in FY26 as digital losses shrank.

history.event: Advent International invests Rs2,475 cr in Apollo HealthCo through CCPS; Apollo HealthCo buys Keimed shares.
history.impact: CCPS of Rs2,457 cr booked as a liability in consolidated borrowings (Screener borrowings up from Rs5,333 cr to Rs7,864 cr in FY25).

history.event: Composite scheme announced: demerge pharmacy distribution + 24/7 + telehealth into Apollo Healthtech (NewCo), merge Keimed into it, list it; 195.2 NewCo shares per 100 Apollo shares.
history.impact: Apollo's shareholders will own 59.6% of NewCo (42.1% directly, 17.5% through Apollo). Shareholders approved on 24-Jun-2026; NCLT sanction pending.

history.event: Promoter Suneeta Reddy sells 1.9 mn shares (1.32%); promoter holding falls from 29.34% to 28.02%.
history.impact: Small, but the second family sell-down since 2019 (promoters held 34.4% in Mar-2019).

history.event: Apollo buys out IFC and other minorities in AHLL for Rs1,273 cr; AHLL becomes 100% owned. IFC's put option (liability of Rs684 cr) extinguished.
history.impact: Cash outflow pushed the company to net debt of Rs866 cr at Mar-26 from net cash; removes a minority leak from AHLL.
history.src: AR FY26 notes 21 and 55; Q4FY26 call

history.event: Four new hospitals commissioned (Pune, Sonarpur, Gachibowli, Defence Colony; ~855 census beds) and Sarjapur-1 acquired; labour-code provision of Rs19 cr.
history.impact: New-hospital losses (~Rs41 cr in Q4FY26) start to weigh on the hospital margin.

history.event: Apollo Cradle and Fertility to combine with Cloudnine at ~Rs1,550 cr (~35x EBITDA); CCI approval 1-Sep-2026.
history.impact: AHLL loses ~Rs450 cr of revenue (24% of FY26) and gets ~Rs750 cr of cash plus a 9.9% stake in Cloudnine.

history.event: Board approves Price Waterhouse as statutory auditor for five years from the 2027 AGM, replacing Deloitte Haskins & Sells.
history.impact: Rotation at the end of Deloitte's term; no qualification reported.

governance.relatedParty: Keimed (promoter-linked wholesaler) supplied Rs968 cr of goods to the group in FY26 (Rs813 cr in FY25) and is being merged into NewCo at a swap ratio set by the board; Apollo's shareholders get 59.6% of NewCo for HealthCo, Keimed's owners 25.3%.
governance.pledge: Prabhudas Lilladher (14-Aug-2026) shows promoter shares worth Rs8.67 bn pledged, ~1 mn shares or ~0.7% of the company (~2.5% of the promoter stake); in 2018-19 promoters had pledged most of their holding.
governance.auditor: Deloitte Haskins & Sells (unqualified FY26 opinion); Price Waterhouse to take over after the 2027 AGM.
governance.landDispute: Karnataka revenue department cancelled the land grant of Imperial Hospital (Bengaluru) in Feb-2026, arguing the share purchase by Apollo alienated the land; the High Court stayed the order on 10-Apr-2026.
governance.src: AR FY26 (remuneration table, related-party note, note 53); PL Q1FY27 note

accounting.indAs116: EBITDA is post-Ind AS 116: lease rent (Rs85 cr in Q1FY27, ~Rs291 cr of lease payments in FY26) is excluded and shows up as right-of-use depreciation and lease interest (Rs174 cr of lease finance cost in FY26). Lease liabilities Rs2,834 cr (Mar-26), Rs2,877 cr (Jun-26).
accounting.ccps: Advent's CCPS in Apollo HealthCo (Rs2,457 cr) are classified entirely as a liability (equity component negligible) and as current, as management expects conversion within a year.
accounting.esop: HealthCo ESOP charges (Rs118 cr in FY26, Rs10 cr in Q1FY27) are inside EBITDA; group share-based pay was Rs159 cr in FY26.
accounting.delhi: The Delhi hospital (Indraprastha Medical Corporation, 22.03%, listed) is an associate: its beds and patients are in the KPIs but only its profit share is in the accounts.

regulatory.text: The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health (176th report, laid on 7-Aug-2026) recommended benchmarking private-hospital room charges in metros to nearby three-star hotel tariffs, ending room-category-linked pricing of procedures, standard package rates, mandatory cost estimates and an independent regulator. Hospital stocks fell up to 3%. These are recommendations, not law; such changes typically take 1-2 years if adopted.
